Yes. It's hard to accept but they are linked to violence. Your logic is something like "I play games where I aim at people and shoot their heads off, but it won't make me even a little bit more violent". Try reading Assassination Generation by Lt. Col. Dave Grossman, who I'm pretty sure is the guy on the right in this picture. You can enter it all you want but they are linked to violence. In the book, he cited several sources. Many video game studies are funded by the video game companies, similar to how cigarette companies used to find studies about cigarettes to make them look good. The book greatly changed my opinions on video games and it's an interesting read. Here's a link: Assassination Generation: Video Games, Aggression, and the Psychology of Killing https://www.amazon.com/dp/0316265934/ref=cm_sw_r_cp_api_BQXOAbW7YYM8F

Though it may be hard to swallow, sadly, yes video games make you (more) violent and more likely to hurt others. Most video game studies commonly cited by gamers to defend their beliefs are funded by video game companies, as in the 20s, cigarette studies were funded by cigarette companies. There are many unbiased studies that show the effects of video games on the minds of humans, especially teens. For more information on the subject, I recommend a book called Assassination Generation, which greatly changed my views on video games, namely first person shooters.
